details:
The friends list pulls it's data from the list of IDs in the user's JSON object that gets returned on the user api call. Some of these IDs may produce 404 errors.

Whether these are deleted, banned, or for some other reason, no longer valid accounts, they will attempt to ping, and return nothing. The issue is that the friends list will still count it in the total friends listed.

This means that if you are pinging for users 30-40 on the website, and one of the users returns nothing, you will only be served 9 users, but the counter will tick up 10 users.

My friends list has 14 of these dead accounts. It's fine if there is a valid reason for them being there, but the website should display the correct number.
title: Friends list not displaying correct amount.

details:
In short, currently, if you post a link to some vrc web page, web services will not generate fancy preview images and descriptions for it. If you look at links to users or worlds you will NOT get ANY info at all. If you look at instance link you will not be able to understand instance details. That's because VRC web site pages lacks for metadata, so web services does not understand about what is the pages. Lack of metadata also affects integration into search engines and it's "relevancy score". My suggestion is to implement common metadata vocabularies protocols to achive better integrations, such as:
- The Open Graph Protocol ( https://ogp.me/ )
- Schema.org ( https://schema.org/docs/gs.html#schemaorg )
- Dublin Core Schema ( https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc5013 )
- Semantically-Interlinked Online Communities ( http://rdfs.org/sioc/spec/ )
- FOAF ( http://xmlns.com/foaf/spec/ )
- oEmbed ( https://oembed.com/ )
- Twitter Cards ( https://developer.twitter.com/en/docs/tweets/optimize-with-cards/overview/summary )

Currently there is OGP and Twitter metadata on the pages, but it's completely static: does not differs from page to page, which makes no sence.
title: Properly Implement metadata on pages to improve VRC integrations into other web services. (Fancy previews!)

details:
Current version: VRChat 2020.3.2p4, build 982
Problems:
1)"Created too many sessions for that user"
When trying to log in from too many places, this happens.
There could be multiple reasons : logging in from multiple browsers,
using different wifi, vpn, your ip dynamically changing, etc.
This security "feature" does not allow you to log in until all active sessions expire.
Most often suggested solution is to wait for a few hours but
I saw a few people who could not log in for days.
It's hard to reproduce but logging in from many browsers and steam client at the same time
and changing between different ips and re-logging everywhere could cause the issue.

2)Active sessions do not expire on password reset
If account was compromized, what do you do? Reset password.
And it does not invalidate currently active sessions.
That's a security concern. And in case of "Created too many sessions for that user" bug affecting you
even password reset would not give you back access to your account.

3)There's no apparent way to log out on all devices
There should be a way do that as a "log out everywhere" button
or / and a list of currently active sessions you could manage and clear.
I think It's possible to protect yourself in case of compromise by changing password,
turning on 2fa and turning it back off but it's a hacky workaround if all you want to do
is invalidate currently active sessions. I'm not sure whether it clears them completely
but even if it does it does not allow you to do that if you can't log into your account
cause you got "Created too many sessions for that user" error.
title: Fix session management

details:
I am trying to find information about the blend shapes / shape keys / pose morph / etc. necessary for avatar animation in VRC and I wasn't able to find anything in the official documentation about
vrc.blink_left
vrc.blink_right
vrc.lowerlid_left
vrc.lowerlid_right
From what I have gathered searching online, I found that the order of these blend shapes is crucial (in this order and these must be the first 4 in the list) regardless of the names given to those blend shapes. This is in reference to VRCSDK 2, and I'm aware that some of this has changed in VRCSDK 3 (i.e. the number and order might be different), but it has been difficult to find official documentation about how to program the non-viseme (e.g. eye "tracking" or blinking) blend shapes for VRC at any rate.
I had to ask around and search a lot before I was able to find the information I needed about this specific behavior, and I would like to see documentation added for this because I think that it could prevent some confusion.
title: Missing documentation about eye tracking / non-viseme blendshapes

details:
If a user is present in an invite only instance (and they are not the instance creator), they are able to vrchat.com: click on the instance they are currently in, and share the invite short link. 
Any user with that link can then click "invite me" to invite themselves, effectively making all instance privacy modes moot, so long as you have an "insider".
While it's wildly convenient in other modes, it has potential for abuse - and users are typically in an invite only world because they want to control the flow of inbound users to prevent bad actors, or they're running an exclusive event with a "leader".
I hope this is addressed prior to the implementation of any guild system.
title: "Invite Me" link is sharable for anyone in an invite only instance.

It's censored. not a bug
try to write "chilloutvr" in your bio

Writing the country name of "Hungary" (where i live) mess up my whole bio, removing formatting and messing up the words

We fixed "amazing" a while ago! Thank you for the report.

If you come across other cases like this, please let us know!

"G↋n" still gets mangled. And judging from below, many other cases of this sort of mangling have been reported. So closing the ticket just because "amazing" was fixed is a bit premature. This ticket isn't resolved until the filtering is removed, IMO.

@{5a4b034d1ab4366d42644996|full_name} This canny wasn't really clear and focused, especially regarding the sentence 'You are amazing'. Technically, it has been completed. However, I believe we need clarification about how the censoring system works. If it is by design, we could make a feature request so the system could be more transparent to the end user, for example it can display an error message "This bio contains forbidden words" instead of messing the whole bio.

Thanks for speaking up! Like @{60c0e22718009c104862d5bc|full_name} said, it's more helpful if each Canny request focuses on a specific issue. Otherwise, user votes would become less useful.

@{5a4b034d1ab4366d42644996|full_name} - The text you posted contains the character "TURNED DIGIT THREE", Unciode character U+218B.

It's a duodecimal digit in math. I think unusual Unicode characters are often filtered for security reasons, or because it would be too difficult for VRChat to support every Unicode character.

@{63691297469f06772579fe6f|full_name} it did focus on a single issue, until VRC staff merged several other word filter failure reports into this one, including general ones that aren't about a specific word, such as "Bio Censor Filter Removes Spaces, Capitalization, and Formatting when changing Bio In-game"

@{6219f63f55639e536dc83162|full_name} I opened a follow up Canny that is more focusing on the profanity filter system here:

https://feedback.vrchat.com/feature-requests/p/profanity-filter-improvements

@{63691297469f06772579fe6f|full_name} Well, _supporting_ every Unicode character - not so hard, just stop blocking them. I've worked for a company as a developer in a context where we had to support internationalised text of all kinds before - it isn't impossible, it's just hard. Competent developers can do it. Do VRChat hire any?

_Rendering_ every Unicode character, somewhat harder.

Note that "supporting" and "rendering" are not the same thing. If you show the character as a square box, that can be considered supporting it correctly. Solving the problem of having a font which contains the character is a next step thing. Not showing the character at all, or filtering it out, is just incorrect behaviour.

Nonetheless it's a character I have in all my bios everywhere else, but VRChat is unnecessarily blocking it. Whether you personally consider it worth using or not is sort of irrelevant - it's already in use, by me, right now, pretty everywhere other than VRChat.

And no, "security reasons" has never been, and will never be, an acceptable reason for having bad internationalisation in an application.

At least you have done the research, though. Turned digit 3 (↋) is indeed used to mean "eleven" in dozenal circles. That is exactly the meaning I have used it for in "G↋n" - the digit eleven stands in for omitting the middle eleven digits of "Globalisation".

details:
The websocket that updates the friends list & the list of worlds your friends are in remains connected so long as you do not switch pages. As soon as you go to any other page, the websocket disconnects & is not replaced. The only way to reconnect it is to refresh the page. This started sometime in early January. Prior to then, switching pages did not cause a permanent disconnect. 


If the websocket closes under any *other* circumstances (it seems to time out naturally once an hour or so) a new websocket is successfully made to replace it, as expected.


Steps:
1. Start out on any page of the website.
2. Click on anything that will cause a page switch. (a user, anything in the side bar, etc)
3. The websocket is now disconnected & friends list / world list will no longer update without a page refresh.


Pictures of the websocket in the inspector's Network panel before & after a page change below.
title: Websocket dies on page changes and is not replaced

details:
At the bottom of the home page "Hey, Have You Seen This Completely Random World?" when clicking the "Load More Worlds" it fails after the 5th world. The index goes 01, 011, 0111, 01111 and finally crashes at 011111.

This is most likely due to it being incorrectly parsed as a string and JS therefore does append rather than increment. The endpoint then fails due to the index being higher than the max limit of 10,000. This generates a Cloudflare HTTP 1020 Access Denied error and causes the button to load forever.
title: Random world fails after 5th world due to incorrect offset increment

details:
Making VRChat worlds more discoverable is essential for creators.  However, the main link to VRChat worlds right now requires a login.  The only way for worlds to be viewable without a login is to create an instance link, and then make sure to only copy the long version, as the short link expires. As you can imagine, this is not intuitive for creators just looking to promote their content. 
  The instance link also does not contain essential info such as player cap, download size, tags, and ***platforms supported***.
I would suggest that any world link from a not-logged-in user should not redirect to the login page, it should redirect to a publicly-viewable version of the world, with better world info, and a prominent "Login to visit" type call to action button.
The use for this is to allow easier access for external discoverability, such as review sites, press, social media, etc, in order to bring people into VRChat to view specific content.
title: Viewing VRChat world info on the website requires login

details:
Deleting friend requests seems like it's not working properly on both ends. In the event that a user sends another user a friend request, and the sender cancels the friend request, the recipient will receive a message from the websocket to remove the notification from the UI, but refreshing the page will make it come back when it asks the API for the current set of notifications. Also the “Cancel Friend Request” button on the senders end will never go away. 

If the recipient of the notification declines the friend request, then the notification will actually delete, but the API will still treat viewing each other’s profile as if the friend request still exists, as “outgoingRequest” is still returning true for the sender, and “incomingRequest” is still returning true for the recipient from the friendStatus endpoint. The only way I can see to exit this state is if the recipient visits the sender’s profile, and clicks “Accept Friend Request”, where the users will now be friends despite the friend request being deleted.
title: [API] Deleting friend requests does not appear to work properly.

Can you describe the "invite yourself glitch"? Being able to invite yourself via the VRChat Home website and launch links is intended. Getting into an instance in this way doesn't permit you to bypass the normal user limit.
Remember that the displayed capacity is the "soft cap" of a room. You can actually fit 2x the number of the soft cap (aka, the "hard cap") before you start getting "the room is full" messages on join.
As an example, Spookyghostboo's The Black Cat has a capacity (or "soft cap") of 18. However, with a link to the instance (or by joining off friends), you can fit up to 36 people in the instance before additional joiners start getting "the instance is full" messages.

title: Gallery upload error text incorrect

comments.body: The only places this is returned in the API is explicitly from checking the file size. If you are still certain this is an actual error, please provide an example image.

@{5ac57845180a7e323c02d48d|full_name}: I've just tried it again at the time of this post. I can verify that this image yields the error mentioned. I'm also uploading this as a photo, not an icon, so the error message is a bit confusing there too.
Edit: Less modified version compared to the attached file: https://i.imgur.com/pXy8ceL.jpeg

@{5d458c2bce0d0218577b8c24|full_name}: Thanks, I will check this out in a moment. The duplicate error message is likely an error on my part when creating the profile picture api code, as it shares the same backing as icons for the most part.

@{5d458c2bce0d0218577b8c24|full_name}: Actually, I just realized why this is happening before I even saved your picture. The image gets sent through the cropper during the upload process, even if you don't touch any of the controls. Once you move onto the next stage of the uploading process, the cropper will duplicate the image, applying the needed transformations, which in this case is none, but is likely resulting in a much higher-sized image buffer being sent to the API.
I'll create a bug ticket for this internally, but as a workaround for the moment, you should be able to downsize your image a bit below 4k to get through the issue.
Thanks for the help in finding a super weird edge case!
@{5ac57845180a7e323c02d48d|full_name}: Thanks! Resizing the image before upload as a workaround also seems to work.

comments.body:
First I thought this was a hidden message from the manager saying, "From now on, it doesn't matter if you are Quest or PCVR, you can post in the same category!"
Certainly, it was very chaotic and should have been fixed, with bug reports, Open Beta and Future Requests all jumbled together in just one category, "Quest Creators" for all this time.
But even if my guess was correct, it is still a great disappointment to lose all the ongoing submissions that had been submitted in the past and had received many votes.
In particular, the post "Add constraint to the whitelist in Quest", which was persistently requested and which the manager commented that he would consider in the future, especially needs to be reinstated.
Here I propose two options.
1. restore the category for Quest and create some new sub-categories (bug reports, requests, etc.) within it.
2. close the Quest category and announce to the community that "Quest and PC categories are now merged!" 
With both of options, I think rescuing lost posts is what the community is looking for.
Please consider it!
This change doesn't appear to have been intentional, it's been fixed now. Thanks for letting us know!
@{5b2821f1443b6a55287c67ad|full_name}: Thank you for the fix!　Each post within https://feedback.vrchat.com/trust-and-safety-system was also no longer viewable, is this intended?

details:
There are two strange bugs that can occur on (temporarily)  suspended accounts. 
1) The VRChat website can sometimes show a blank black/greyish screen (see screenshot) when  attempting to visit vrchat.com/home instead of the usual sign-in screen. From the looks of it, it is possible that the website is attempting to log in the user before the login screen is shown, as the 403 message can be found (with the json suspended message) in the browser's JavaScript console. For the average user, this can make it difficult to review the ban reason or the number of days until the suspension expires from outside the client. 
2) The canny is *still* fully accessible and functional provided you were logged in before the suspension and you visit feedback.vrchat.com directly rather than vrchat.canny.io (from my experience, this always sends you to the oauth page, which cannot be used by suspended accounts). This was marked as "complete" in an earlier post but is still an issue.
title: Suspended account weirdness

details:
Over the past couple months, I've noticed that the updating a world does not properly tell the API that it was updated. On multiple occasions, I have uploaded an update to my world but it didn't appear in the "Updated Recently" section, and the website had an out of date "Last Updated" date. 
Strangely, updating twice within a short timeframe (a few hours) fixes this. I found this when I needed to apply a hotfix shortly after a major update. Both times I ended up doing this the world "updated" status was not changed until the second upload of the day.
It's worth noting that updating the description or title of a world via the website gives it the "Recently Updated" tag immediately, without needing to do so twice.
title: API "Updated Recently" status for worlds seems to be broken

comments.body:
I remarked this too - but a little bit different: It looks, like the "Last updated" date is only updated, when you are also listed in the "Updated recently" list. 

If you do daily updates for example (which is usual, when your world is still in develeopment), then you will be blocked from this list (for a duration of 5 days or so). This makes probably sense, because some creators would use it to stay permanently on that list. But this blocking mechanism seems also to suppress the "Last Update" date, which is bad, in my opinion. Users should be able to see, if the world was updated.

@{5f2eaed841e042066f65cb45|full_name}: Yes there definitely seems to be some blacklisting system behind the scenes, where if you update your world too frequently you are no longer allowed the Updated Recently tag.

For me, it seems to have been permanent. I actually made a support ticket about it once and they manually gave me the Updated Recently tag, but seemingly didn't remove my world from the blacklist. I usually put out one big update every month or so, and maybe a few patches or hotfixes shortly after.

I think the "Updated" date should at least be updated every time. For my world if you just look at the last "updated date" it says Oct 2022, making it appear to have been stagnating for a while despite having relatively consistent monthly-ish updates.

@{5baf2b2de038c00e28fd16b5|full_name}: It seems, that I ran in this permanently block for one of my worlds too.

During development, I had almost daily uploads without issues (world was set to "Private"). After realease, I had some short intervalled patches. The "Updated" entry started to stuck then. Today, I uploaded a new patch after 3 weeks of pause. The "Updated" entry is still Dec 27 and my world doesn't appear in the recently updated list today.

As creator, you spend a lot of time to build worlds and serve a good quality to players. But if some short interval quality updates blocks you totally from that "Recently Updated" list, you will have no attention anymore. And if users checks your world page, it looks as your world is dead, because of the wrong "Updated" entry. 

It's absolutely ok, that creators cannot spam the "Recently Updated" list and there is some cooldown time. But block worlds forever and not refresh the "Updated" entry, will probably disencourage developers to continue on their projects. The bad thing also is - you will not be notified, if your world is currently blocked.

@{5acad9ecc9dba010c9c3ec68|full_name} 

Hi Tupper - can you please take an eye on this and clarify, what creators can do, to not run into this problem? What we have to do, to unblock our worlds from this (probably permanent) block.

details:
As the title says, when someone other than myself builds an instance of Invite or Invite+ on the web and presses Invite Me to enter the instance, I usually receive an Invite from myself, but now I do not receive any Invite at all. Of course, I am friends with the instance owner.
I can Invite Me without any problem for Invite or Invite+ instances where I am the owner, and I can also Invite Me for Friend Only instances where the owner is my friend. The problem occurs when you Invite Me to an Invite or Invite+ instance where your friend is the instance owner.
Perhaps this problem has occurred since the Secure Instance update a while ago. Previously, Invite Me was possible without any problem even if the friend was the instance owner's Invite or Invite+ instance. This is very inconvenient for certain purposes, for example, when socials are not updated properly, or when you want to share a private world with several people, each at his/her own time.
title: Invite Me not received for Invite and Invite+ instances where someone else is the instance owner

- It's a red button. Red buttons are associated with dangerous actions on the website (Unpublish, Delete world, Delete account), but clicking this button subverts expectation as there is no confirmation dialog
- Clicking the button doesn't just remove all "messages" from the website, it removes all received friend requests themselves causing "Friend Requests" list from the "Social" tab in-game to effectively disappear as it is emptied. It is unclear that "Friend Request" in the social tab is actually considered being equivalent to a message. For example, if you receive a notification on Android for a new mail, clearing the notification does not mean archiving the mail in the app nor marking it as read; there is a distinction between a notification of a mail and the mail itself, which is not the case here.
- The message counter on the website maxes out at 100, but clicking the button will remove all friend requests, which can go in the thousands.
- Clicking doesn't put the friend requests into the "Ignored friend requests" list, which is yet another unclear behavior that makes it seem like it differs from declining the friend request
title: Clarify what "Clear all messages" does on click

details:
When uploading an image to be used as a profile picture, in most situations either through the website or in-app it'll be heavily compressed and the image resolution drops, most notable when looking at your profile picture up close. I've noticed the only way to get around this is as follows.

`1.) Go to VRC Website > Gallery > Photos`

`2.) Click 'Upload Photo'`

`3.) Upload any 16:9 photo, 1920x1080 might be preferable here.`

`4.) On 'Preview before upload' screen, make sure 'Set as profile picture' is checked. Upload photo.`

`5.) Open VRChat and go to your profile, observe your profile picture up-close and notice it's high resolution.`

This is the only way to ensure your profile picture is displayed in high resolution, whereas if you were to select another already uploaded image from your gallery, that profile picture would be much lower resolution.
title: Profile pictures get heavily compressed in certain situations

details:
As it is currently, the localization strings do not have glossary entries for VRChat concepts like "Visitor".

This will make it so that translations containing these words will confusingly use different vocabulary in each sentence that uses them. It is not particularly helpful for other language users if the UI shows one word for "Visitor", and the tooltips/explanation show another word, despite them being the same in English.

Indeed, I can already see this happening in the Japanese translation, and it probably is happening in the other languages as well.

When I used to do translations for Discord (back when they still used Crowdin), they used the 'Glossary' function to mark concepts. This makes the definition of the concept, and optionally a chosen equivalent per language, come up wherever the word appears in the localization files.

VRChat's project should be using this feature to ensure the vocabulary is consistent, else if it is too confusing I feel as though people will just discourage the use of translations (given they have figured it out up to now anyway).
title: VRChat Crowdin needs glossary words to be marked

details:
Navigating vrchat.com/home using a keyboard (or a different similar assistive tool) is pretty much broken or unsupported. 

This is an important aspect for accessibility or just people who use keyboard to navigate around.

Steps to reproduce:

Use TAB to navigate around the website, there are many different problems along the way.

Most prominent problems:

**Many interactive elements do not have a focus indicator or it's barely visible.**

- E.g. left menu buttons, favorite avatars list filter dropdowns, "Invite me" in Friends wing, and many more.

**Some elements are inaccessible through keyboard navigation or are just not using semantic elements like <button> or <a> or tabindex attribute to even be focusable.**

- (Some JS messing stuff up) Try TABing to the notifications button, hit ENTER to interact with it, a panel with notifications opens, but you cannot keyboard navigate anymore. There are now errors popping up in console with each click of TAB.

- Favorite avatars -> Edit Mode -> cannot tab to "Add to selection", because it's a <div> (it's nice that it has "aria-" and "role" attributes, but it doesn't make it focusable, there are more examples like this).

- accept/cancel/etc.. "buttons" (they are <div>) in notifications, and more.

**Many interactive elements miss alt or title attribute.**

These are just a few examples
title: (Accessibility) Keyboard navigation is really bad

In the past, there used to be more options in the 'Blocks & Mutes' management section of the VRC website. Why they removed these options I have no clue, but there was one that was VERY important to me.

To try keep this short, my internet connection and VRC don't get along well. If I load more than 2 avatars at a time, the vrchat servers will decide that I don't meet their standards for internet quality and serve me a timeout error (despite still seeing and hearing everyone fine and the downloads coming through fine). 

To get around this, I have EVERY avatar hidden by default via safety settings and manually, one by one, show my friends when I join a world.

The issue here is that, at the end of a long weekend, I now have a lot of people manually shown. If I join on these friends later and more than 2 of them are shown and wearing a new avatar, I will time out again. I need to re-hide their avatars to not time out.

I used to be able to mass-revoke the 'show avatar' flag using vrchat's website, but it has been removed for a number of months now, leaving me to manually hunt down every person I saw that weekend in-game to reset their avatar status from 'shown' to 'use default (hidden)'.

Please return the button you removed to the vrc website.

On the avatar web page, the "Publish Avatar" and "Switch to Avatar" buttons are nearby, but they should not.

I think "Publish Avatar" should be placed near the "Delete Avatar" button and have a warning color.

In addition, "Publish Avatar" button will publish the avatar immediately, but I think VRChat should confirm if user actually want to publish avatar with dialog.

These two buttons have very different risks.

Switching avatars is low risk, just wearing the avatar.

On the other hand, publishing avatars has a high risk of violating Terms and Conditions of the model file.

For most commercial assets for avatars, It's not allowed to publish an avatar for everyone.

That's why "Publish Avatar" should be placed near the "Delete Avatar" button and have a warning color and VRChat should confirm if user actually want to publish avatar with dialog.

Nowhere in the Community Guidelines does it state anything about sexual activity itself, however it does prohibit publicly sharing the content (as you can see from the attachment). details:
The website uses the following API endpoint to populate the Group Member List:

groups/{groupId}/members?n=25&offset=0

This endpoint takes in two query  params: n (number of users to get) and offset (number of users to skip over before starting to list them).

When this latter offset value is higher than 5,000, an error such as the following is returned:

{"error":{"message":"offset＝5100 is much too high․ refine your search you savages․","status_code":400}}

The message in this error code seems to imply that this error was intended to prevent requests of member blocks that are too large. However, this condition is being applied to the offset parameter as well, which is unrelated to the size of the request.

As a result of this, the Group Member List page on the website will stop working after scrolling through 5,000 users.
title: Website Group Member List stops working after 5,000 users

```

However, according to https://ogp.me/, meta tag for OGP should use `property` attribute.

For services that supports twitter card to get website information, fall backed to twitter card which is currently correct but for services doesn't support that (e.g. misskey, A fediverse SNS, doesn't support twitter card by bug), they fails to get website information.

details:
When you search for certain users with common or popular names (lots of similar duplicates) the search results that return sometime do not show the user you are looking for despite the account being active. We either need the search results to be longer, or we need the search results to show multiple pages, or the ideal solution would be to allow us to search using the user ID (Or simply ban directly by UserID). That way we can find the exact person we need to ban immediately.

Example:

details:
# Problem

Browsing the vrchat.com/home website can end up in favorite worlds endpoint blocking you out because of too many requests (screenshots #1 #2 #3). This results in favlists dropdowns and fav/unfaving button not working properly (screenshots #4 and #5). This happens to me every time when I try to unfav a world or two to fav a new one.

# How to reproduce

[User perspective:]

In general it happens for me all the time when I open up the website to fav a world, but often I find my world favlists to be full, so I open favs to look for worlds to unfav, then try to fav the new world.

[Tech perspective:]

You can also just open a world view page, then refresh a couple of times, and you'll see that there's a bunch of https://vrchat.com/api/1/favorites?n=XXX&offset=XXX&type=world happening and often the last few of them failing due to 429 Too Many Requests. Especially if you fav or unfav a world, because that single action also makes ~19 requests for the world favlist(!!!) and it's easy to combo with the similar ~19 requests happening right after loading the page.

I believe the endpoint might have too restrictive request limits, seeing how similar spams of e.g. friend list endpoint are just fine.
title: Browsing favorite worlds ends up with "Too many requests" all the time for me

details:
# Issue Announcement images currently do not scale properly, due to the use of ``. Instead, `background-image` on the parent DIV should be used, alongside `aspect-ratio` in portrait mode. # Problematic Code Example - Landscape ```
``` - Portrait ```
``` # Fixed Code Example - Landscape ```
``` - Portrait ```
``` # Explanation - Not all rendering engines handle `` sizing the same way as `
`; In WebKit, for example, a height of `100%` inside a flex-item causes the flex-item the image is within to **scale to the height of the parent container.** The image is sizing to *100% the parent container and not the immediate parent which it is within.* - DIVs however scale normally, and, for the seemingly desired implementation (image fills DIV, DIV is height of announcement in landscape and the width of the announcement in 16:9 in portrait), setting the `background` property with a separate `background-size` is preferable. - In this case, in both landscape and portrait, setting the `background` property of the DIVs, which originally contained the image, to `no-repeat center ('image-url')` ensures that they display the image as their background, center-aligned. - Setting the `background-size` to `cover` ensures that the image scales to fill the container **without** resizing it. This property cannot be set in the combined `background` property for compatibility reasons. - **In portrait mode**, setting the `aspect-ratio` property of the DIV containing the image to `16/9` allows the browser to intrinsically set its `height` to 9/16ths its `width`. Without this the image has a height of `0`. - **In both cases, the **``** is removed entirely, as it is not needed.** # Environment - macOS Sonoma - Safari 17.3 (19617.2.1.11.3) - WebKit # Attachments - Before and after pictures of an announcement, displaying both the problem, and the results of the fix.

https://vrchat.com/home/launch?worldId=wrld_6caf5200-70e1-46c2-b043-e3c4abe69e0f&instanceId=ArcticLucky_AI~group%28grp_7c75c192-e00e-4ac8-a14b-95bcbfa8429b%29~groupAccessType%28public%29~region%28us%29

Shout-out to Nekromateion who figured out what is wrong: https://github.com/vrcx-team/VRCX/issues/767#issuecomment-2048547628

The (same) issue is present when you try to use the VRChat website to invite yourself to the instance.

The API request fails and returns a 400 error, but the website doesn't handle this and simply displays the checkmark regardless.

The endpoint that is used is (already in your original message so I figured you'd know).

`/api/1/invite/myself/to/{WorldIdWithInstanceId}`

The endpoint attempts to validate the InstanceID but that filter only checks for alphanumerical and the "_" causes it to mark the InstanceID as invalid.

details:
There exists a method in which anybody can launch group public instances for any group, even if they do not belong to that group. This was confirmed to be the case with the permission turned off for the "Everyone" role. This does not require any tooling, external programs, direct access to the API, or changes to the VRChat client. This includes groups that are closed and invite-only. The only exception to this is if the member is already banned from the group.

What does this actually mean for you?

- Malicious instances could be opened in opposition to a group's values. For example, a group supporting those who have PTSD from war would not want a group public instance opened in a warzone map.

- Groups that only open moderated instances by policy could have public unmoderated instances opened on their behalf without approval.

- Groups representing staff or brand ambassadors could have public instances opened on their behalf without approval.

I initially informed VRChat of this on 09/11/2024 via the App/Website Security Exploit Report form under ticket #441683. Per the form: "We do not guarantee a response other than the automated "ticket received" notification." And that's all I've gotten. Unfortunately, this means that I have no way of knowing if VRChat is still actively aware of this exploit, if they plan to take ownership, or when a fix is expected. 

Precautions you can take as group owners:

Monitor your instance lists. Also monitor your audit logs in Settings -> Logs via the group page on the VRChat website.

I have intentionally left out the method, but it is trivial and only a matter of time before others figure it out, if they haven't already. Staff can check the ticket provided for the method.
title: Missing permissions check on group public instance creation

details:
**Title:** "Website Does Not Reflect 'Appear as User' Visual Rank Setting"

**Description:**  

The "Appear as User" setting, which is available in the VRChat application, does not reflect correctly on the VRChat website. This setting allows users with ranks from "Known User" and above to toggle their displayed rank to appear as a "User" for personal or privacy reasons. While this change is applied correctly in-game, the website continues to display the actual rank of the user (e.g., Known User, Trusted User), even after logging in.

**Steps to Reproduce:**  

1. Log in to the VRChat application.  

2. Enable the "Appear as User" option by clicking your trust rank below your status.  

3. Log in to the VRChat website and navigate to your profile page.  

4. Observe that the rank displayed on the website does not update to "User."  

**Expected Behavior:**  

When the "Appear as User" setting is enabled in the VRChat application, the website should display the user's rank as "User" to match the in-game setting.

**Actual Behavior:**  

The website continues to display the user's true rank (e.g., Known User, Trusted User) rather than reflecting the "Appear as User" setting applied in-game.

**Additional Details:**  

- The issue is specific to the website and does not impact the functionality of the setting within the application.  

- This inconsistency may lead to confusion for users who expect their website profile to align with their in-game settings.
title: Website does not reflect 'Appear as User' visual rank setting

details:
I'm constantly finding explanations of various functions available through udon to be a bit vague or leave out information or have "secret" problems... or require a lot of extra blind testing to find out what they do... some examples...

OnPlayerLeft(VRCPlayerApi player) "Fired when a player leaves the instance"

But will it fire for the player who left? Or is it only firing for the people who are still there? That's an important detail so I know if I can cleanup things for that player when they leave, or if I need to do it another way.

VRCPickups ->

OnPickup

Is this firing ONLY when I pick it up, or is it firing when ANYONE picks it up?

Some functions like OnPlayerTriggerEnter fire when anyone activates it, but I think OnPickup is different and only fires when YOU activate it... but I keep forgetting! I tested OnPickup multiple times before... but now it's been a while and I forgot which way it behaves... now I have to test it again to make sure... and it takes me so long to recompile and test...

Well, in short; A small note like, "this will fire for all players" and "this will fire only for the interacting player" will be useful!

---

Speaking of "OnPlayerTriggerEnter ", I've heard there's a lot of inconsistencies with it or situations where it and OnPlayerTriggerExit might not work - from what I hear "exit fails on many cases like stations, avatar change and sometimes just randomly".

I don't know if these are bugs but this is important information, and even if it is a known bug, it could be listed as one explaining all the fail cases or proposed alternative (using bounds check).

https://creators.vrchat.com/worlds/udon/players/getting-players/

"Above, you can see the bare minimum for a working call to GetPlayers. A better approach would be to construct VRCPlayerApi[] as a variable so you can reuse it."

I am thankful for the example, but confused why someone would write an example, and then immediately say, "But there is a better way to do it that we didn't use for the example".

I think a function example showing it being set up and used in a for loop to do something would be most helpful.

----

I was going to reply about how OnPlayerTriggerEnter also fails randomly when a player is teleported into it.

But then I found out that this actually IS mentioned on THIS page:

https://creators.vrchat.com/worlds/udon/players/player-collisions

Personally, I think the note about the edge cases where it fails should be highlighted in red! It is pretty crucial that we know it isn't reliable at all.

It also seems like players have figured out more of the edge cases, so more could be added to the list.

Tbh, now I wonder if there are situations where it's 100% reliable at all? Is it really at the very least reliable when physically walking slowly into it?

----

I also noticed that pages under the "creators" prefix have a "Feedback" button... which I'm glad to submit feedback to!

However, there is another page referencing OnPlayerTriggerEnter, which is the main page where I was actually finding the names of these functions to use while learning how to use UdonSharp.

https://udonsharp.docs.vrchat.com/events/

There is no "Feedback" button on this page, and this page is missing a lot of those important details - rather is the inspiration that I make this post in general.
title: Better wiki data

details:
When a role is deleted from a group, the users who had that role assigned retain the now-defunct role ID in their data. This leads to two key problems:

1. These users do not show up under "Users with no role" in the group management UI, even though their role is technically invalid and not displayed.

2. There is no official method to remove these stale role IDs via the UI or standard workflows. The only current workaround is to manually interact with the VRChat API to clear the role assignment from each affected user.

This situation can cause confusion for group administrators, as users with invalid roles may be effectively "invisible" in the role management filters, and there is no clean way to remove the broken assignments.

It would be very helpful if role deletion also cleaned up references to that role in user assignments, or at least provided an interface for detecting and resolving these orphaned roles.
title: Group role deletions don't clean up assigned role IDs on users

details:
There's an isolated issue with invm_95b3441b-308a-4083-bd26-e3b57dc61cf3 on my account usr_6fa4abc5-9952-4a0a-97de-b3598fbf6a5c which prevents one specific invite message (message slot 6, "Let's party!") from being updated, due to the [June 8, 2025 API instability/outage incident](https://status.vrchat.com/incidents/jsv0xj6rztl3). (Full details are available in the support ticket: #591843)

## Expected behavior on message slot 6 update (success scenario)

The invite message is updated, canBeUpdated is set to "false", updatedAt date is updated, remainingCooldownMinutes is set to 60, and the API responds 200 OK.

In the VRChat client, the message "Updated message text" should appear, and the message is expected to be updated.

## Alternative expected behavior on message slot 6 update (failure scenario)

The API should respond with a HTTP response code 500 Internal Server error or similar, or returns an error message in the body JSON response. I don't expect the API to respond 200 OK in this scenario.

## Actual behavior on message slot 6 update (failure scenario)

The invite message is not updated, canBeUpdated remains "true", updatedAt date is not updated (remains at old value "2025-06-08T01:12:29.649Z"), remainingCoolDownMinutes stays at its previous value 0, and the API responds 200 OK.

In the VRChat client, the message "Updated message text" appears, and the message in the UI resets to the previous message from 2025-06-08T01:12:29.649Z (the old message received from the API). (Video: https://files.catbox.moe/co6xpw.mp4)

---

Unofficial API reference:

- https://vrchat.community/openapi/get-invite-messages

- https://vrchat.community/openapi/update-invite-message

- https://vrchat.community/openapi/get-invite-message

API requests and responses are attached as text files (with small redactions to personal data relating to login cookies and User-Agent identity for the public; unredacted versions are in the support ticket).

- Message slot 5 update (`4 - Update message 5.txt`) is included for a demonstration of the expected PUT behavior.

- Message slot 6 update (`5 - Update message 6.txt`) is included for a demonstration of the unexpected PUT behavior.

- `7 - Get Invite Message 6.txt` contains the singular GET response from the API for message slot 6.
title: API may (incorrectly) respond HTTP/2 200 (200 OK) to the client when updating an invite message fails silently in the API server backend

details:
The calendar's event creation form on the website defaults to having an event start time 24h after time of loading. Also, it refuses to let you set a start time that's in the past. As a result, when you try to change the date portion of the start time from the next day to the current day, the change will not "stick", because such a time is considered to be in the "past". No feedback is provided to the user explaining what's happening. This results in events being scheduled incorrectly.

Currently the only way around this is to set the time before setting the date to the current day. But this is contrary to how most people think, not to mention the date is always displayed before the time and if you're using your keyboard, you tab to the date before tabbing to the time.

I suggest instead of setting the default start time to a confusing (hard to notice) and broken 24 hours after the current moment, it should be set such that the time is at least five minutes after the current moment (regardless of what the default day is). Personally I'd use one hour after the current moment, in the current day. This solves the problem (assuming the user takes less than one hour between starting event creation and setting the start time, which seems reasonable) without requiring a change in the start time restriction rules.
title: [Calendar] Creating an event for the same day is unintuitive/broken (UI)

details:
Thank you for your continued work on the development and maintenance of VRChat.

The [UI Events documentation](https://creators.vrchat.com/worlds/udon/ui-events/) lists the methods and properties that can be called from uGUI events such as **OnClick** and **OnValueChanged**.

However, it appears that there are some items which are actually allowed but not included in this list.

For example, `TextMeshProUGUI.text(string)` can currently be invoked through uGUI events, yet it is not mentioned anywhere in the documentation.

There may also be other properties or methods that are permitted but not currently listed.

Because of these discrepancies, it can be difficult for creators to determine whether a call is officially supported or simply working by coincidence.

If possible, it would be greatly appreciated if the documentation could be updated to include **all currently allowed UI Event targets**, ensuring that the list fully reflects what is supported in practice.

Thank you very much for your time and consideration.
title: There seem to be missing entries in the UI Events (uGUI allowed list).

details:
When creating an event on the calendar, if the date is in the future (which it usually will be), then the date validation will fire off on every edit, which means that it will constantly revert the date to the default end time.

For example, if it is currently 11/14/2025 at 2:43 AM and I try to create an event from 11/21/2025 from 2 PM to 3 PM, and I enter the correct start date, then when I try to edit the end date, when I enter 11/21, it sees that the default-set end time of 3:43 AM is before the start time and then reverts the editor to 11/14/2025 3:43 AM. And if I try editing the time first, it sees that the date makes it invalid. So what I end up having to do is set the end date several days ahead (e.g. 12/01/2025), then edit the time, then edit the date.

It would be much better if the input validation didn't reset the entire editor when there's an error, especially since it already indicates an error with the red box anyway. That should be sufficient validation before submission!
title: Setting an event end date is needlessly difficult

details:
If the owner of a VRChat group assigns themselves to a custom role that requires Two-Factor Authentication while their account does not have 2FA enabled, the website locks them out of all group management actions.

Because the user is the owner:

- They cannot delete the group (requires 2FA).

- They cannot change their role (UI blocks all actions until 2FA is enabled).

- They cannot disable the 2FA requirement on the role.

- They cannot leave the group because owners cannot leave.

Steps to reproduce:

- Create a group.

- Create a custom role that requires 2FA.

- Assign this role to yourself (the owner).

- Do not have 2FA enabled on your account.

- Try to edit settings, change roles, or delete the group.
title: Group owner becomes locked out after assigning self to 2FA-required role without having 2FA enabled

details:
It is possible to launch a Friends/Friends+, or Group Public instance under someone else's name without needing their credentials. This could be used in malicious ways.

For example, a group may only allow their group moderators to launch new instances, but it is possible that anyone can launch a group public instance, and even under someone else's name who is not a group moderator - and all it takes is the launch URL.

A malicious user could use a world that contains exploits to steal user data, for example, and create a group public instance without any perms needed to create a sense of trust of a group's members to go visit it, who may think it is a legitimate instance by the group.
title: Instance Launch via Web URL exploit

details:
Currently, the ability to view and unban users are tied to the ban user permission, configurable via the api or the website.

This disallows groups from allowing a role to accept appeals without also permitting them to sabotage the group, in the event of malicious behavior.

Example:

The "Remove User from Group" permission is already separated - good.

However, if a user has the "Manage Group Bans" permission - they can bypass that by simply banning people from the group by username, which of course then removes them from the group.

This is both a vulnerability to the permissions system, as well as an inconsistency that makes it difficult to create effective management roles for the group.

I recommend splitting it into three permissions, and making "Ban from group" additionally require "Remove user from group".
title: VRCAPI Permissions "Manage Bans" -> "View/Unban/Ban".

details:
I currently have MULTIPLE crasher and NSFW avatars reported via the in-game/website ‘Report’ option which remain publicly available weeks after their being reported.

Multiple attempts to address this via T&S with the requested ‘additional evidence’ are only met with the same generic ‘use the in-game’ boilerplate response and closure of the ticket, despite the text of the ticket pointing out that has already been done.

“If you would like to attach any evidence alongside your report, please resubmit it through the Helpdesk form.”

These ARE the followups your boilerplate message is asking for.

Jan. 08, 2026   https://help.vrchat.com/hc/en-us/requests/653874

Jan. 27, 2026  https://help.vrchat.com/hc/en-us/requests/659622

A more recent ticket was to report a KKK avatar, in which I pointed out that the avatar was too new to appear in the standard avatar search, so the in-game/website report function was impossible to use in this circumstance.  So I included logfile which show the avatar's name and the username of the uploader.

Feb. 06 2026  https://help.vrchat.com/hc/en-us/requests/662660

This received the standard boilerplate response and closure of the ticket literally seconds after it was submitted.

I decided to try moving it up the chain, and submitted what you see above to the Help Desk to report that I was having trouble with the website.  Instead of a 'Submit' button, I was instead met with a 'Next Step' button, which feeds my ticket to an AI Assistant to attempt solve the issue without having to bother a human being.

“Our Help Desk assistant will scan through our docs and check to see if we can help you right away. If you still need assistance, you can submit a ticket to our User Support team.”

It dissected my message, reiterated all of my points and broke them out into bullet points, then added some flowery platitudes while repeating the 'use the in-game' mantra.  Ultimately admitting that there is no workaround or way to escalate a report with the ticket system. 

It then says that if this did not address my issue, to go ahead and click Submit so someone could address it.    So I did.

Today, the ticket received this....

-----------------------

Hello,

It looks like you may have sent a moderation-related inquiry to the incorrect channel.

If you would like to resubmit your report, we encourage utilizing VRChat’s In-app reporting system. For more guidance, please refer to the following articles:

- Blocking, Unblocking, and Reporting Users in VRChat

- Reporting Avatars and Worlds

- Reporting Groups

If you would like to attach any evidence alongside your report, please resubmit it through the Help Desk form.

Lilith

VRChat Team

-----------------------

This new “smooth transition into a newer, more streamlined report system” is more akin to a brick wall if the report doesnt fall into a very narrow set of defined violations, with no room for special case outliers.  (outliers that are far too common)  It is utterly demoralizing for those who want to help make VRChat better/safer.

details:
The following help desk article URL has an incorrect/outdated statement: https://help.vrchat.com/hc/en-us/articles/360062658133-I-can-t-see-anyone-s-avatars

> Very Poor avatars are always performance blocked on VRChat Mobile. At this time, users running the Mobile app cannot show (or wear) them.

This help desk article was last updated more than a year ago, and hasn't been updated since. Formerly [it used to be that Very Poor avatars were blocked on mobile completely back in 2024](https://old.reddit.com/r/VRchat/comments/1hkahgy/very_poor_avatars_on_mobile/m3dtwuk/), but this restriction has been since relaxed.

The statement is contrary to actual behavior in-app today (and in the past for a while now) and documented behavior in VRChat Creator documentation, which states Very Poor mobile avatars can be forcefully shown on mobile: https://creators.vrchat.com/avatars/avatar-performance-ranking-system/#mobile-default-performance-rank-blocking

> For example, if a mobile avatar exceeds 20,000 triangles, it's "Very Poor" and users can't see it in VRChat. However, users can forcefully show "Very Poor" avatars by selecting the user and clicking "Show Avatar".

Very Poor mobile avatars can also be worn. Only a few (3? 5?) Very Poor avatars will be shown at a time on mobile platforms currently.

Suggested change: Update the help desk article to remove mentions of wearing Very Poor on mobile, update the article to mention the current restrictions on viewing [X] number of Very Poor avatars on mobile, and include the warning from VRChat Creator documentation about VRChat possibly removing "Very Poor" mobile avatars in the future.
title: Help Desk article "I can't see anyone's avatars" mistakenly states "users running the Mobile app cannot show (or wear) [Very Poor avatars]"

details:
I don't know if the change was intentional or not, but with the rollout of the revamped web profiles, the 18+ Verified badge was silently removed from them, and we need it back.

Many groups who offer age-gated instances, including my own, offer VRC+ verification alongside regular manual ID verification for people who have already verified themselves through VRC+. We want to offer age-gated instances without forcing users to pay up for a subscription, so doing age checks and granting a role to access specific instances was a fair middle ground.

Groups like mine rely on the Verified badge being able to be seen on the website, otherwise we won't be able to offer VRC+ as an alternative verification method and have to manually ID verify every person who wants to attend the age-gated instances. If they're already visible in-game, why not on the website too?
title: 18+ Verified Badge no longer visible on web profiles

details: After creating a recurring event series, if you delete any individual occurrences from the series, the series still creates an event series entry on the originally scheduled days that no longer have an occurrence when the time that the event would've started approaches. details: The World Favorites tab in the Website provides a feature that lets users to select multiple worlds and execute Delete or Move actions, but this feature does not work properly. For example, if I select over 30 worlds and try Delete favorites, the progress bar often stops halfway through, and the process does not complete. Looking at the status code, it returns a 429 (Too Many Requests) error.
